symptom: On iPhone Safari, pricing/lifecycle and monthly/yearly controls rendered but taps produced no state change. The language selector showed 'Switching language failed. Try again.' and the page remained Dutch.
root_cause: Pricing bound click handlers directly to the initial button nodes. The shared mobile shell can replace or recompose DOM after those handlers are attached, leaving visible replacement buttons without listeners.

The language runtime redirected canonical unprefixed pages to /en/<route>. Release builds deliberately set STATIC_I18N_NETWORK=0, so when the static translation cache is incomplete the English route is not emitted. The selector could therefore navigate to a route that does not exist.
fix: Move pricing state handling to an external cache-busted runtime with document-level delegated click, change and input handlers.
Switch canonical unprefixed public pages between NL and EN in place using the existing runtime translation endpoint and persisted bg_locale state.
Keep static /nl and /en routes supported when present, but never require them for the interactive language toggle.
Cache-bust i18n.js from the site-wide injector.
prevention: Interactive public controls that must survive shell recomposition use delegated event ownership or explicit rebinding after replacement.
A user-facing language switch may not depend on a build artifact that offline release policy can legally omit.
Mobile browser regression must click affected controls and verify resulting DOM state changes rather than only checking that buttons render.
evidence: Public /prijzen exposed the language error text while remaining Dutch.
Production pricing source used direct per-node click listeners in bg-pricing-neno-v1-js.
build-localized-routes.mjs returns no English route output when STATIC_I18N_NETWORK=0 and translation cache is incomplete.
The candidate adds assets/js/pricing-interactions-v4.js, in-place i18n switching and mobile click assertions in verify-targeted-website-routes.mjs.
